learnings.remediation: a dependency-table key with a package value is a local alias: read the real name from spec['package'] and keep the alias out of the identity
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 11/20: serde1 = { package = "serde" } reported an unrelated crate named serde1

learnings.remediation: keep the declared spec verbatim; only an exact == pin collapses to its version, and a purl carries a version only when the spec pins one
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 8/12: lstrip('=<>~! ') made demo!=1.0 report 1.0 and ranges read as resolved pins

learnings.remediation: read every declared section - npm's four tables, PEP 621 optional-dependencies, PEP 735 dependency-groups, Poetry main/dev/groups, Cargo main/dev/build/target - before calling the inventory complete
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 6/15: this repo's own [dependency-groups] produced no rows and no gap

learnings.remediation: a depth walk that skips ahead past a match must re-enter at the matched delimiter or the walk's balance drifts and every later candidate in the same region sees the wrong depth - consume delimiters exactly once, wherever the fast path lands
learnings.source: greptile round-19.6: the set-state walker jumped past setX( ... ) including its '(', so a second setState statement in one effect body saw paren == -1 and stayed silent

learnings.remediation: discovery must match the advertised filename pattern (requirements*.txt as a regex), never an exact-name list
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 5/14: requirements-dev.txt and requirements-test.txt were never parsed and produced no gap

learnings.remediation: a parser boundary maps every failure class it can raise to the handled class before the scan entry: ElementTree reports an unknown declared encoding as LookupError, not ParseError (and LookupError is not a ValueError), so catch (ET.ParseError, LookupError) at the reader and pin the property with a hostile-input battery through scan_sbom - every unreadable manifest a gap with a reason, nothing escapes - not one crafted example
learnings.source: pr-24 round-19 finding 2: one csproj declaring encoding=unknown-encoding stopped the whole inventory

learnings.pattern: slow scan|anchor count.*rout|routing by count|gauge tables.*entire file|2\.34s|scan cost grew with file length, not similarity
learnings.remediation: a fast path chosen by a count misprices alignments whose real work is small - measure the work instead: sample a few candidates' actual cost, scale it, and take the fast path only when the measured cost outweighs the fast path's own fixed price; pin both directions with a sentinel test and a budget test at the reported scale
learnings.source: greptile round-19.6 finding 1: the prefix-gauge routing keyed on 16 anchors, so 276 alignments of 24 files sharing a 20-line helper built 4,000-line tables (2.34s) for walks that finish in 0.016s

learnings.remediation: a writer whose output is a committed file must satisfy the repo's .editorconfig - the learnings store renders indent=2, and tests/test_ci_learnings.py pins the writer's own bytes to the padding/final-newline contract, not just the committed copy
learnings.source: hosted hygiene red on round-19 fix 12c9b04: the store's indent=1 render put 16 odd-padding lines into .github/master-ci-learnings.json and editorconfig-checker failed the master and happy-path hygiene jobs

learnings.remediation: a check keyed on a naming shape collides with the stdlib and with methods - gate on the shape plus the discriminator the real API implies (a React hook setter is a bare identifier, not obj.setter) and name the collision set outright (setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate); run every gate past a flag-list and a quiet-list before shipping
learnings.source: greptile round-19.6: the set-state-in-effect shape matched setTimeout, listener arrow bodies and store.setState before the bare-identifier, nested-arrow and named-exemption gates

learnings.remediation: tests document contracts, not invented incidents; any artifact a review shows is byte-verified against disk before it enters release history
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 22/24/25: a rendering artifact was written up as a shipped outage; the strip-then-compare test would have blessed the mangling

learnings.remediation: a scan that must map a regex match back to a line cannot read over a collapsing strip (it moves every offset) - blank string and comment contents in place, length preserved, and run the match on the masked copy with offsets intact
learnings.source: greptile round-19.6: the no-new-array scan first read over _strip_strings, whose single-space replacement would have reported every match at a drifted line

learnings.pattern: AttributeError: ('list' object has no attribute 'items'|'NoneType' object)
learnings.remediation: validate the decoded object and its section shapes before use and raise ValueError, so the scan records a data gap instead of stopping
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 4/26: package.json as [] or a dependency table as an array stopped the whole scan

learnings.remediation: npm scoped names keep the %40 escape, Go module paths and NuGet ids keep declared casing; identity rules are per ecosystem, never one shared lowercase
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 10/19: @types/node became pkg:npm/types/node

learnings.pattern: grow[s]? every anchor|one growth per anchor|long clones? stall|1\.8s|quadruples with (their |the )?length
learnings.remediation: growing one anchor is an integer random walk (match -1, mismatch +3, alive while 4*misses - k <= 2): prefix the diagonal once as G[v] = 4*misses - v and every anchor's stop becomes a last-under / first-over range query - identical blocks, no per-anchor re-walk; pin the optimization with a seeded differential test against the direct walk on every diagonal shape plus a wall-clock budget on a 4,000-line near-copy pair
learnings.source: pr-24 round-19 finding 1: two 4,000-line near-copies took ~1.8s of repeated growth during every scan

learnings.pattern: debug-prnit|not a live check id|typo.*clean row
learnings.remediation: external labels are validated against the live check registry (slop_model.REMEDIES) before judging; a typo is a configuration error, never a vacuous clean row
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 finding 23: debug-prnit: clean always scored a correct clean result

learnings.remediation: an undeclared-import check must trust every site the resolver trusts before pricing a specifier: every manifest in the tree (dep sections plus the package's own name), tsconfig/jsconfig paths prefixes at segment boundaries, # subpath imports, and a scoped specifier's two-segment package - anything else is a false positive on the project's own layout
learnings.source: greptile round-19.6 user evidence: the check priced @/ aliases, #app/config, @scope/pkg/plugin and monorepo members as undeclared packages because it read only the root package.json

learnings.remediation: dependencies carry NOASSERTION; the manifest's license is a project license reported separately, never stamped onto dependency rows
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 1/17: an MIT application made unknown-license deps pass deny_unknown

learnings.pattern: split_case\(case\)|row labels ignore (the )?ratio|counts mix (both splits|training and holdout)
learnings.remediation: judge per case id (the fixture slug the manifest assigns) and read each row's split from the already-computed manifest; never re-hash the case under a default ratio
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 2/3/16/18: stats keyed by rule merged both splits and contradicted the report's own manifest

learnings.remediation: grow every candidate and keep the best (most matched evidence first, then score, then earliest start); one alignment still reports once
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 13/21: min(anchors) let a shared import preamble hide a 14-line near-copy at the same offset

learnings.remediation: manifests scanned from arbitrary repos are untrusted input - stdlib ElementTree expands entity bombs (measured: 30,000 characters from a four-level nest), so the csproj reader parses through defusedxml and fails closed to a recorded gap when the safe reader is absent; it never falls back to entity expansion enabled
learnings.source: semgrep pr-24 alert 441 (error severity): the new csproj reader imported xml.etree.ElementTree, one new code-scanning alert red-flagged Semgrep OSS on the pull request

learnings.remediation: parse XML by element and attribute names (ElementTree, namespace-tolerant): attribute order, quoting, extra attributes and child Version elements are all ordinary references
learnings.source: greptile pr-24 findings 7/9: the Include-first regex silently dropped valid references
